context.context: On November 15, during a pivotal council session held at the Wilson Building, D.C. Public Schools Chancellor Kaya Henderson laid out her controversial plans to close 20 city schools. This meeting drew significant attendance from council members and concerned parents, highlighting a looming battle over school boundaries and access to quality education in the D.C. area. Henderson emphasized that these closures would be part of a broader strategy to revise school boundaries and feeder patterns for the first time since the 1970s, a move expected to invite intense scrutiny and political debates across the city. The implications of the proposed changes resonate particularly in affluent neighborhoods, where access to top-performing schools is a significant concern for families. Activists and parents express fears that these alterations will disproportionately affect poorer and minority students, limiting their access to quality education and exacerbating existing inequalities within the D.C. public school system.
